tips.title: Know your CPF accounts
tips.summary: OA, SA, MA, RA — four accounts, four jobs.
tips.details: Your monthly CPF contribution splits into Ordinary Account (housing, education, investment), Special Account (retirement), MediSave (healthcare), and Retirement Account (formed at 55 from OA+SA). Below 35, the split is roughly 23% OA, 6% SA, 8% MA of your wage. Knowing where each dollar goes helps you plan housing down payments, hospital bills, and retirement income separately.

tips.title: Top up your SA/RA for tax relief
tips.summary: Up to S$8,000 self + S$8,000 family = S$16,000 tax relief.
tips.details: Cash top-ups to your own Special Account (under 55) or Retirement Account (55+) earn dollar-for-dollar tax relief up to S$8,000/year. Top up parents, spouse, siblings or grandparents for another S$8,000. SA earns 4% risk-free, beating most fixed deposits. Caveat: top-ups are irreversible and locked till 55/retirement age.

tips.title: Watch your MediSave Basic Healthcare Sum
tips.summary: Once MA hits BHS, overflow goes to SA (or OA after 55).
tips.details: The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the cap on your MediSave Account, adjusted yearly. In 2026 it's around S$77,500. Any contributions beyond BHS spill into your SA (before 55) or OA (after 55). Track this so you don't accidentally over-top-up your MA when chasing tax relief.

tips.title: Pick the right CPF LIFE plan
tips.summary: Standard, Basic, or Escalating — trade-off is payout vs bequest.
tips.details: At 65 you start CPF LIFE payouts. Standard = higher level payouts, smaller bequest. Basic = lower payouts, larger bequest. Escalating = starts ~20% lower but rises 2% yearly to fight inflation. Default is Standard. You can switch once before payouts start, so revisit this in your early 60s.

tips.title: BTO vs Resale: pick your trade-off
tips.summary: BTO is cheaper but waits 3-5 years; Resale is now but pricier.
tips.details: BTO: subsidised price, 99-year lease starts fresh, but ballot luck and 3-5 year wait. Resale: move in within months, mature estates, pricier but eligible for Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (up to S$80k) and Proximity Housing Grant. Compare total cost including renovations, MOP impact, and your timeline.

tips.title: Respect the 5-year MOP
tips.summary: Sell or rent out the whole flat? Wait 5 years from key collection.
tips.details: Minimum Occupation Period is 5 years for most HDB flats, counted from key collection (excluding any time you sublet or stayed overseas). During MOP you can't sell, rent out the entire flat, or buy a private property. Renting individual rooms is allowed with HDB approval. Plan life events (kids, upgrades) around this.

tips.title: HDB loan or bank loan?
tips.summary: HDB: stable 2.6%, higher LTV. Bank: lower rates but volatile.
tips.details: HDB concessionary loan: 2.6% (pegged to OA+0.1%), 75% LTV, no penalty for early repayment, income ceiling S$14k. Bank loan: rates often 3-4% but fluctuate, only 75% LTV first loan, lock-in periods, but no income ceiling. Bank loans suit those with stable income and risk appetite; HDB loans suit conservative buyers.

tips.title: Cash Over Valuation is real
tips.summary: Hot resale flats need cash on top — CPF/loan can't cover it.
tips.details: When a resale flat sells above HDB's valuation, the difference (COV) must be paid in cash. CPF and loans only cover up to valuation. In hot estates COV can hit S$50k+. Ask for valuation before negotiating, and budget cash separately from your down payment.

tips.title: First S$20,000 chargeable income is tax-free
tips.summary: Singapore has one of the lowest personal income tax rates globally.
tips.details: Resident tax rates are progressive: 0% on first S$20k chargeable income, 2% next S$10k, rising to 24% above S$1m. Use reliefs (CPF top-up, SRS, course fees, parent relief, NSman) to lower chargeable income. File via myTax Portal between Mar 1 and Apr 18 each year.

tips.title: SRS: cap your tax bill, invest the contributions
tips.summary: S$15,300/year (citizens/PR) of tax relief, withdraw at 63+.
tips.details: Supplementary Retirement Scheme: contribute up to S$15,300/year (S$35,700 for foreigners), get full tax relief on contributions. Cash earns 0.05% — invest into stocks, bonds, REITs or single-premium insurance instead. Withdraw from statutory retirement age (63 from 2026), only 50% taxable. Don't open the account until you're ready to contribute — your retirement age locks at first contribution.

tips.title: Check NFS before scrambling to file
tips.summary: If you're on No-Filing Service, IRAS auto-files for you.
tips.details: Most employees under the Auto-Inclusion Scheme don't need to file — IRAS sends a Notice of Assessment by Sep. But you must verify reliefs and report side income (freelance, rental, crypto trading as a business). Log in to myTax Portal in Mar/Apr to confirm. Underreporting income gets penalties up to 200% of undeclared tax.

tips.title: MediShield Life only covers B2/C wards
tips.summary: Public hospital subsidised wards. Anything more, get IP.
tips.details: MediShield Life is mandatory and covers large public hospital bills at subsidised B2/C ward rates. For A/B1 wards or private hospitals, you need an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) on top. IPs come from 7 insurers; premiums rise sharply after 50 — lock in young while healthy. Always check the rider for co-payment caps.

tips.title: CareShield Life pays for severe disability
tips.summary: Lifelong monthly payouts if you can't do 3 of 6 daily activities.
tips.details: Auto-enrolled at 30 if born in 1980 or later. Pays out monthly for life if you become severely disabled (can't do 3 of: bathing, dressing, feeding, toileting, mobility, transferring). Premiums fully payable by MediSave. Top up with supplements from Aviva/Income/Singlife for higher payouts.

tips.title: Term insurance, not whole life, for most
tips.summary: Buy term, invest the difference. Cheaper, simpler, more cover.
tips.details: A 30-year-old non-smoker pays ~S$30/month for S$1m term cover till 65. Whole life for the same sum costs 5-10x more. Term gives you maximum protection during your earning years; invest the savings into low-cost index funds. Re-evaluate cover when you marry, have kids, or take on a mortgage.

tips.title: Park 6 months of expenses in a high-yield account
tips.summary: Singlife / UOB One / OCBC 360 / Chocolate — ~3-4% on idle cash.
tips.details: Before investing, build 3-6 months of essential expenses in a liquid account. High-yield savings (Singlife, Chocolate Finance, MariBank) and bonus interest accounts (UOB One, OCBC 360, DBS Multiplier) currently pay 3-4% on caps S$50k-100k. Beats fixed deposits and is instantly accessible.

tips.title: SSB and T-bills for safe yield
tips.summary: Government-backed, beats fixed deposits, redeemable monthly.
tips.details: Singapore Savings Bonds: 10-year step-up bond, redeem any month with no penalty, up to S$200k holding limit. 6-month T-bills: auctioned every 2 weeks, recently 3-3.8% yield. Both fully backed by SG government. Apply via DBS/UOB/OCBC ATM, internet banking, or SRS funds for tax-sheltered yield.

tips.title: Index ETFs beat stock-picking for most
tips.summary: VWRA, IWDA, S27 — boring, low-cost, decades of compounding.
tips.details: Use Interactive Brokers, Tiger, or moomoo to buy globally diversified ETFs. VWRA (LSE-listed accumulating world ETF) avoids US estate tax. Local: STI ETF (ES3/G3B) for SGD income. Avoid US-domiciled ETFs (VOO, VTI) for non-US persons due to 30% dividend withholding and 40% estate tax above US$60k.

tips.title: Robos lower the bar to start investing
tips.summary: StashAway, Endowus, Syfe — auto-rebalance from S$1.
tips.details: Robo-advisors charge 0.3-0.8% to manage diversified portfolios. Endowus is the only one that lets you invest CPF-OA and SRS into unit trusts at wholesale fees. StashAway and Syfe accept cash and SRS. Compare TER (total expense ratio) — robo fee + underlying fund — before deciding. Cheaper than commission-based advisors.

tips.title: Stack one cashback + one miles card
tips.summary: UOB One for groceries/utilities, DBS Altitude for travel.
tips.details: Most people overcomplicate credit cards. Pick one cashback card for everyday spend (UOB One, Citi Cash Back, OCBC 365) and one miles card if you travel (DBS Altitude, Citi PremierMiles, KrisFlyer UOB). Hit the minimum spend, pay in full, never carry a balance — interest is 26%+ APR.

tips.title: Singles can BTO at 35 — any flat type
tips.summary: Since 2024, singles can apply for any HDB flat type, any location.
tips.details: Since the Oct 2024 rule change, singles 35+ can buy 2-room to 5-room BTO/resale flats in any estate. Income ceiling S$7,000 for BTO singles. Resale grants for singles capped at half of family rates. The Joint Singles Scheme lets you co-own with another single 35+.

tips.title: SimplyGo with credit card = no top-up needed
tips.summary: Tap your contactless Visa/Mastercard at the gantry.
tips.details: Skip the EZ-Link card and tap any Visa/Mastercard contactless card or phone wallet at MRT/bus gates. Charges deducted daily. Some cards rebate transit spend (UOB One, Citi SMRT, Trust Cashback). Concession card holders should still use the physical card for fare discounts.

tips.title: Owning a car? Budget 1.5x the price
tips.summary: COE, ARF, road tax, insurance, parking, ERP — it adds up.
tips.details: A S$120k car easily costs S$200k+ over 10 years after COE (~S$100k+), ARF, road tax, insurance (S$1.5-3k/year), petrol, parking (HDB season ~S$100/month), and ERP. Compare with public transport, taxis, and car-sharing (BlueSG, GetGo) before committing. COE is non-refundable on early de-registration.

tips.title: ROM in 21 days — file the notice early
tips.summary: Online filing, S$42 (citizens), 21-day notice + ceremony slot.
tips.details: File Notice of Marriage on ROM's website 21 days to 3 months before the wedding date. Solemnisation can be at ROM (S$26 weekday/S$300 weekend) or external venue with a licensed solemniser. You'll need both NRICs, two witnesses, and pre-marriage prep course if either party is under 21. Update HDB, CPF, IRAS afterwards.

tips.title: Claim Baby Bonus within 12 months
tips.summary: Cash gift up to S$11k + government-matched CDA up to S$4k.
tips.details: Cash Gift: S$11,000 for 1st-2nd child, S$13,000 for 3rd+. Child Development Account (CDA): government matches your contributions up to S$4,000 (1st), S$7,000 (2nd), S$9,000 (3rd-4th). Open the CDA at OCBC/UOB/POSB. Funds usable for childcare, MediSave, healthcare. Apply via LifeSG app within 12 months of birth.

tips.title: NSmen: claim relief and stay IPPT-ready
tips.summary: S$1,500-5,000 NSman relief + IPPT incentives up to S$500.
tips.details: Operationally Ready NSmen get S$1,500 relief annually (S$3,000 if called up that year). Wives and parents of NSmen get S$750 each. Pass IPPT for up to S$500 cash, plus continued reservist eligibility. Track via NS Portal. Plan ICT leave and pay make-up claims early.

tips.title: Make a will AND CPF nomination
tips.summary: CPF doesn't follow your will — nominate separately.
tips.details: Without a CPF nomination, your CPF goes to the Public Trustee and gets distributed by Intestate Succession Act, with admin fees. Make an online nomination at cpf.gov.sg in 10 minutes. Separately, draft a will (DIY templates from MoneyOwl/Singlife or hire a lawyer ~S$200-500) for property, investments, and bank accounts.

tips.title: Sign an LPA while you're healthy
tips.summary: Lasting Power of Attorney — appoint someone to decide if you can't.
tips.details: An LPA names trusted people to make personal welfare and property decisions if you lose mental capacity. Form 1 is free for citizens (cert fee ~S$75). Without an LPA, family must apply for a deputyship via court — costly and slow. Submit via OPG online portal with a certified issuer (doctor/lawyer/psychiatrist).

tips.title: Compare retailers on Open Electricity Market
tips.summary: Switch from SP Group default to save 10-30%.
tips.details: Since 2018 you can choose your electricity retailer (Geneco, Keppel, Senoko, etc.). Fixed plans lock in a rate; discount plans give a % off the regulated tariff. Compare on the OEM website. No service disruption when switching — same wires, same SP meter, just different billing. Watch contract length and early termination fees.

tips.title: Use Healthier SG for free screenings
tips.summary: Enrol with a GP, get heavily subsidised chronic care.
tips.details: Healthier SG lets you enrol with a regular family doctor at a polyclinic or participating GP. Free recommended health screenings (blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, cancer screens) and vaccinations. CHAS subsidies stack on top. Enrol via HealthHub app — takes 5 minutes.

tips.title: Use your SkillsFuture credit before it expires
tips.summary: S$500 base + S$500 (40+ top-up) + S$4,000 mid-career.
tips.details: Every citizen 25+ has S$500 baseline credit (no expiry). Singaporeans 40+ got an extra S$500 (expires 31 Dec 2025) and S$4,000 mid-career credit (specific approved courses, expires Dec 2026 unless extended). Use for Coursera, Udemy SG, polytechnic CET, or SkillsFuture-approved bootcamps. Plan ahead — refunds for incomplete courses are limited.

tips.title: Negotiate your starting salary — once
tips.summary: Annual increments compound off your starting base.
tips.details: Singapore companies usually have S$2-5k flexibility on offer. Use MOM's salary data, Glassdoor, levels.fyi as anchors. A S$3k bump on a S$80k base is S$36k+ over 10 years assuming 3% raises. Negotiate sign-on bonus or AWS too — they don't compound but help year one. Don't accept on the spot; ask for 24-48 hours.

tips.title: Tenants pay stamp duty on the lease
tips.summary: 0.4% of total rent for leases up to 4 years.
tips.details: Stamp the tenancy agreement within 14 days of signing via IRAS e-Stamping. For a S$3,000/month 2-year lease, stamp duty = S$3,000 x 24 x 0.4% = S$288. Either party can pay (usually tenant). Unstamped leases aren't admissible in court if disputes arise. Keep the certificate.

tips.title: Second property = 20% ABSD for citizens
tips.summary: Plus property tax bracket spikes if not owner-occupied.
tips.details: Citizens: 0% ABSD on 1st residential property, 20% on 2nd, 30% on 3rd+. PRs: 5% / 30% / 35%. Foreigners: 60% on any. Non-owner-occupied property tax brackets are 12-36% (vs 0-32% owner-occupied). Decoupling, trust structures, and dual-key units are common workarounds — but each has costs and risks.

tips.title: Polyclinic for chronic care, GP for speed
tips.summary: Subsidised but slow vs full-price but in-and-out.
tips.details: Polyclinics: heavily subsidised consults (S$15-20 for citizens, less for kids/seniors), good for chronic conditions, vaccinations, follow-ups. Expect 1-3 hour waits. GPs: S$30-60 walk-in, fast, often open after hours. CHAS Blue/Orange cards give GP subsidies of up to S$28/visit.

tips.title: S$5 hawker meal x 2/day x 365 = S$3,650
tips.summary: Eating out is cheap but adds up. Cook 2-3 times a week.
tips.details: Hawker meals (S$4-7) keep food bills manageable but a daily restaurant lunch (S$15-20) costs S$5,500/year. Cooking even 3 dinners/week saves S$2-3k. Use NTUC FairPrice's house brand and FairPrice Online for delivery. RedMart and Sheng Siong have weekly promos worth tracking.

tips.title: Freelancers: register GST at S$1m revenue
tips.summary: Below S$1m turnover/year, GST registration is voluntary.
tips.details: Self-employed and sole proprietors must register for GST if taxable turnover exceeds S$1m in a calendar year (or expected to). Below that, voluntary registration may help if your clients are GST-registered businesses. File quarterly. Keep separate business accounts and proper records — IRAS audits are not gentle.

tips.title: Self-employed: MediSave is mandatory
tips.summary: Pay MediSave annually based on net trade income.
tips.details: Self-employed earning over S$6,000/year net must contribute to MediSave by April after the assessment year. Rate scales from 4% to 10.5% by age, capped yearly. Pay in instalments via GIRO. Skipping = blocked from renewing licences (e.g. CPFB, MOM passes). Counts toward your BHS like normal contributions.

tips.title: Block scams with ScamShield + Money Lock
tips.summary: Free SPF/MAS apps and bank features that actually work.
tips.details: ScamShield app filters scam SMS and calls. Money Lock (DBS digiVault, OCBC Money Lock, UOB LockAway) ring-fences savings — funds can't be transferred digitally, only at branch with ID. Adds friction that defeats most phishing scams. Set a portion of emergency funds in there.

tips.title: PayNow your UEN, not your NRIC
tips.summary: NRIC PayNow leaks your name; use phone number or UEN.
tips.details: PayNow lookup by NRIC reveals your full registered name to anyone. Link via mobile number instead, and uncheck NRIC linkage in your bank app. Businesses use UEN. Avoid sharing screenshots showing PayNow QR + NRIC. PDPA fines exist but the prevention is on you.

tips.title: CPF Shielding before 55 (if it suits you)
tips.summary: Invest SA out before RA forms, then deposit cash to RA later.
tips.details: At 55, OA+SA up to Full Retirement Sum forms your RA. Some 'shield' SA by investing it into low-risk funds before 55 so the cash isn't auto-transferred — keeping the 4% SA interest cushion. Note: from 2025 onwards, the SA was closed for those 55+ and the 'shielding' tactic's value depends on your goals. Discuss with a fee-only advisor before executing — irreversible mistakes are common.
